title: Surprise-Index Watch
dataSources: Forecasts (`prediction:forecast`), resolved outcomes (`prediction:outcome`), personal bets (`bet:personal`), calibration scores (`calibration:score`), Brier scores (`brier:score`).
app: Personal forecasting and calibration — a private prediction journal of dated forecasts about your own life, resolved outcomes, and calibration / Brier scoring — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=prediction:outcome
| eval surprise=if(result="incorrect" AND confidence>=80,1,0)
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(surprise) as surprises, count as resolved by _time
| eval surprise_pct=round(100*surprises/resolved,1)
| sort - _time
description: Counts the outcomes that genuinely surprised you — confident predictions that turned out wrong — each month.
value: Surprises are the richest learning moments; tracking them makes sure you actually learn from being wrong.
implementation: Ingest resolved outcomes into `index=personal`; count high-confidence misses per month.
visualization: Column chart of monthly surprise rate.
grandmaExplanation: It counts the times life surprised you by proving a confident guess wrong, so you learn from each one.
